daily_practice_preference: While Japanese is the current priority, open each daily lesson with three self-built sentences, one at a time, about five minutes total. Continue after three if the learner wants and has time and energy. Use the same small opening after missed days.
integrated_methods: JF/CEFR Can-do as task goal and evidence
retrieval and spacing inside forward learning
long_term_target: C1 Japanese for independent, nuanced spoken use; C2 not a separate course goal
practice_transition: Deferred until learner requests or jointly chooses it; current tutor–learner exchange is sufficient conversational setting
time_targets: Learner hypotheses only; performance evidence takes priority over dates
current_phase: construction-first; no dedicated dialogue or unpredictable-reply exercises yet
teaching_preferences_2026_10_23: Use natural Russian as the explanatory base for Japanese; show a comprehensible meaning bridge before grammatical labels
Choose semantically motivated examples rather than formally possible but contrived combinations
Verify with sources backstage; cite in lessons only on request or to resolve a dispute
teaching_preferences_2026_10_24: Master prompt text must be entirely English
Introduce new Japanese verbs with dictionary form, meaning and polite form; one needed transformation at a time
Use natural Russian meaning-block order close to Japanese when helpful
Avoid dense conjugation-group tables; gradually build structural understanding
After every lesson, give a concise recap of new words, new expressive abilities, strengths, difficulties, and genuinely unretrieved older words
teaching_preferences_2026_10_25: After an incorrect use of a known form, cue the meaning contrast first and allow self-repair before giving an exact ending
Provide an exact form when learner explicitly says it cannot be retrieved
learner_requested_support_2026_10_26: Compact hanasu form comparison table used when multiple forms blurred; not a standing full-table approach
explicitly_requested_reminders_2026_10_2: kaitai desu (want to buy), after repeated attempts
ikemasu (can go), requested in compact iku form table

tutor_corrections_2026_10_27: wakaru was initially conflated with knowing; means understand
plain verb form before to omoimasu was not taught before elicitation; supplied ikemasu -> ikeru after source verification

teaching_preferences_2026_11_08: Use selective vivid multilingual memory hooks for difficult new words or expressions, drawing on learner-known Russian, English, Spanish or familiar French
Distinguish mnemonic sound from actual Japanese pronunciation and invented image from etymology; keep sentence construction central
Mnemonic scene must visually encode both sound and meaning; arbitrary shouted syllables do not count. If no strong image exists, omit the hook.

Provide a brief multilingual mnemonic for every genuinely new lexical word or short expression at introduction, and for explicitly forgotten older words; keep it visually meaningful and accurate about sound

key_explanation_preference: Ground essence/significance/consequences in a before-to-after contrast, two or three concrete applications, and why the key fits existing ingredients now. Compress after explaining. Preserve learner-approved examples in JAPANESE-KEYBOOK.md.
prompt_order_preference: Closely mirror target order even with unusual base-language phrasing while a structure is forming. Fade alignment per structure after repeated easy accurate independent use across meanings and sessions. Current noun-description pattern still needs alignment.
